introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory to all candidates) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) The rate of change of the radius of a sphere is $2\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$ at the instant when the radius of the sphere is $3$ cm. Find

(a) the rate of change of the surface area of the sphere. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $r$ be the radius. The surface area is $A=4\pi r^2$. By the chain rule (related rates):

$$\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}=8\pi r\times\frac{dr}{dt}.$$

With $r=3$ and $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=2$:

$$\frac{dA}{dt}=8\pi(3)(2)=48\pi.$$

**The surface area is increasing at $48\pi\approx150.8\ \text{cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) the rate of change of the volume of the sphere. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume is $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$, so

$$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}=4\pi r^2\times\frac{dr}{dt}.$$

With $r=3$ and $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=2$:

$$\frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi(3)^2(2)=72\pi.$$

**The volume is increasing at $72\pi\approx226.2\ \text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) The area bounded by the curve $y^2=x^2+1$, the $x$-axis from the origin to the ordinate $x=2$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis. Find the volume of the solid generated. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume of revolution about the $x$-axis is $V=\pi\displaystyle\int_a^b y^2\,dx$. Here $y^2=x^2+1$ is given directly, and $x$ runs from $0$ to $2$:

$$V=\pi\int_0^2(x^2+1)\,dx=\pi\left[\frac{x^3}{3}+x\right]_0^2=\pi\left(\frac83+2\right)=\frac{14\pi}{3}.$$

**The volume of the solid is $\dfrac{14\pi}{3}\approx14.7$ cubic units.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii) Three particles of mass $3$ kg, $2$ kg and $5$ kg are placed on points with position vectors $(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)$, $(5\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)$ and $(4\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)$ respectively. Find the position vector of the centre of gravity of these three particles. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The position vector of the centre of gravity is $\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{\sum m\mathbf r}{\sum m}$.

Total mass: $3+2+5=10$ kg.

Moments (mass $\times$ position vector):

$$3(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)=6\mathbf i+9\mathbf j,\quad 2(5\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)=10\mathbf i+10\mathbf j,\quad 5(4\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)=20\mathbf i-15\mathbf j.$$

Sum: $(6+10+20)\mathbf i+(9+10-15)\mathbf j=36\mathbf i+4\mathbf j$.

$$\bar{\mathbf r}=\frac{36\mathbf i+4\mathbf j}{10}=3.6\mathbf i+0.4\mathbf j.$$

**The centre of gravity has position vector $3.6\mathbf i+0.4\mathbf j$, i.e. the point $(3.6,\ 0.4)$.**
